transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-11-18
- Start: 15:30 PST
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Solace Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (CTO), Ethan Park (Security), Lena Ortiz (Data Eng)
- Recording link: (internal) rwd-recordings/ff-2026-11-18-solace.mp3
- Shared artifacts: Deck: https://bit.ly/rwd-models-deck, Security brief: https://drive.redwood/sec-solace.pdf

Summary:
Solace is evaluating open model options for a clinical triage assistant and patient messaging summarization. Main constraints: long context (20k+ tokens for patient threads), multilingual support (EN/ES/FR), strict PHI handling (want private deployment or VPC), and tool-calling to integrate with internal ticketing. They asked about tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private for latency, cost, and compliance. Agreed to run a dedicated benchmark and exchange anonymized prompts.

Topics covered:
- Model selection: open models vs off-the-shelf APIs
- Context length and chunking strategies (20k-40k token needs)
- Multilingual evals and tokenization differences
- Tool-calling and secure connector patterns (ticketing, EHR lookups)
- Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Security: SOC2/ISO, KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML, data residency

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and Diego's here from our SE team. how's everyone doing?
[00:09] Priya Nair: Hi Maya, doing good thanks, we've got Tom, Ethan, and Lena with me. Busy week but excited to dig in.
[00:15] Tom Reynolds: Yeah thanks, hope we can cover model choice and where to host it, that's the key gating for our PoC.
[00:22] Diego Alvarez: Great, we'll try to focus on the model tradeoffs first — latency/cost/quality — and then deployment. quick question: when you say 20k context, is that bursty or sustained?
[00:34] Priya Nair: Mostly thread-based, like patient conversation history plus records, the average thread tops 12-18k but some go to 30-40k when you include attachments transcribed. so we need something that can handle long context or we need clear chunking with retrieval.
[00:48] Maya Chen: OK that's helpful — Redwood supports models with larger context windows and we also do prefix KV cache and retrieval integration. Diego will talk about how we handle continuous batching and KV cache.
[00:58] Diego Alvarez: Right — so for large sequences we typically recommend either a native long-context model (if available) or a hybrid: retrieval + windowing + KV caching. note that native long-context variants can be more expensive per token but simpler for tool-calling because the tool state can live in the same decoder context. Small pause... like sometimes the transcript tool converts KV cache to "K V cash" in our notes ha.
[01:20] Ethan Park: haha yeah that's the transcription. on security, obviously PHI is a no-go for hosted unless we have a BAA and dedicated isolation — what's Redwood's posture?
[01:30] Maya Chen: We do offer hosted with enterprise controls, but for PHI most customers either use Redwood Dedicated with reserved capacity and VPC peering or Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane / on-prem). we have SOC2/HIPAA guidance; I'll attach the security brief.
[01:44] Priya Nair: For us, latency matters during live triage — sub 300ms token latency for short prompts, and for long-context summarization we can tolerate a few seconds but throughput matters. how do you balance batching vs latency?
[01:57] Diego Alvarez: Good question — Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching tuned by latency SLOs. you set a target p50/p95 and the router will batch up to that window. Dedicated deployments give you predictable throughput and tighter latency SLAs because you control the GPU pool. Hosted is more variable but easier to start.
[02:14] Tom Reynolds: Cost is huge too. our finance team will compare per-token pricing across vendors. do you have examples for a 1M tokens/month workload?
[02:24] Maya Chen: We'll provide a TCO sheet. rough rule: dedicated commits reduce unit cost by 30-50% vs hosted at scale; private on-prem has higher fixed costs but lowest marginal token cost if you own hardware. we'll send a modeled spreadsheet after this.
[02:36] Lena Ortiz: On multilingual — we need EN/ES/FR production quality. are you recommending a single multilingual model or language-specific models?
[02:45] Diego Alvarez: It depends — single multilingual models are convenient but sometimes a language-specific quantized model yields better tone and hallucination reduction. we can run evals on your sample prompts; we also recommend tokenization profiling because Spanish and French can change token budgets.
[02:58] Priya Nair: We also need tool-calling to query our ticketing system and to trigger a follow-up workflow. any concerns about exposing connectors in Hosted?
[03:07] Maya Chen: For tool-calling we support function-style calls. with Hosted you can use secure connectors and Redwood will not log payload if you opt out, but for strict compliance people prefer Dedicated or Private so connectors run inside their VPC and data never touches public control plane. Diego, maybe walk through typical connector patterns?
[03:22] Diego Alvarez: Sure — pattern A: webhook-based calls with short-lived tokens; Pattern B: VPC connector where we establish a private link; Pattern C: on-prem adapter for air-gapped EHR. for PHI we'd push Dedicated with VPC or Private. note that for some customers we implement a signed token exchange so the model calls the function but the private backend validates it.
[03:41] Ethan Park: What's the auditability? we need immutable logs for tool calls and model inputs for audits.
[03:48] Maya Chen: Redwood exposes audit logs with token-level traces, and you can configure retention. for Private you can keep logs entirely in your SIEM. also we integrate with KMS for key isolation.
[03:59] Priya Nair: Model selection: we were looking at LlamaX variants, Mistral derivatives, and some long-context LLMs. any recommendations?
[04:08] Diego Alvarez: Quick take: LlamaX-style open models are great for cost and customization; Mistral family often scores high on generation quality; for long context look at models that support 64k windows or use memory-augmented approaches. Redwood's model catalog tags models with verified perf profiles — we'll share a matrix.
[04:25] Tom Reynolds: Are you doing model quantization by default on Dedicated? worried about quality regressions.
[04:31] Diego Alvarez: We have quantization profiles — post-training quantization can reduce footprint with minimal quality loss but it's model-dependent. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization settings per workload; for critical clinical text we usually suggest higher-precision variants for the PoC.
[04:47] Priya Nair: For the PoC, we want a canary approach: start Hosted for quick iteration, then move to Dedicated for the perf benchmark, and if compliance requires it, to Private. is that typical?
[04:57] Maya Chen: That's exactly the pattern many customers use. Hosted to prototype, Dedicated for scale and SLA, Private when you need on-prem or air-gap.
[05:05] Lena Ortiz: About integration — latency with tool-calls: do calls block the generation? we want non-blocking function calls so we can parallelize lookups.
[05:13] Diego Alvarez: Our tool-calling supports either blocking sync responses or async callback patterns. you can instrument the runtime to continue generation with placeholders and then splice results in, or enforce sync if you need final consistent output.
[05:25] Tom Reynolds: Any red flags with EHR connectors and PHI? we need BAAs and often on-prem adapters.
[05:31] Maya Chen: We have BAA patterns and customers with EHRs use VPC peering or private deployment. we'll share our HIPAA appendix.
[05:38] Ethan Park: Encryption — can keys be customer-managed?
[05:42] Maya Chen: Yes, KMS/HSM integrations are supported in Dedicated and Private. for Hosted we offer bring-your-own-key for certain enterprise tiers.
[05:50] Priya Nair: Let's talk about expected metrics from your benchmarks. what do you report?
[05:55] Diego Alvarez: We provide p50/p95 token latency, tokens/sec throughput, GPU utilization, and cost per 1k tokens under the measured workload. we'll also surface quality metrics: ROUGE/BLEU for summarization and a hallucination score from our eval harness.
[06:10] Priya Nair: Can you run multilingual BLEU/ROUGE for Spanish and French?
[06:14] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we can run language-specific evals — please provide sample references.
[06:18] Maya Chen: Quick logistical thing — what's your timeline for PoC?
[06:21] Tom Reynolds: We want a 6-week PoC starting early Dec, then decision by mid-Jan.
[06:27] Maya Chen: That seems doable. we'll propose a timeline and bench slots.
[06:31] Priya Nair: On the model governance side, how do you support model pinning and rollbacks? we need to ensure reproducibility for clinical behaviors.
[06:39] Diego Alvarez: Redwood supports model version pinning per route, rollout controls with canary/A-B, and automatic fallback policies. all of that is surfaced in the Console and audit logs.
[06:48] Ethan Park: About data residency — some of our records must stay in-region (EU for a subset). can Redwood route by region?
[06:54] Maya Chen: Yes, smart routing by region or tier is supported. you can restrict a route to EU regions only. with Private you of course control exact placement.
[07:01] Tom Reynolds: Competitors — we'd like to see how Redwood compares to Anthropic/OpenAI on latency and cost. can you provide a comparison?
[07:08] Maya Chen: We'll include a competitive slide. generally the difference comes down to model variant and deployment mode; Redwood's value is runtime and ops controls.
[07:15] Priya Nair: Regarding long-context models, do you do partial KV caching across sessions? we have threaded conversations where earlier context is re-used a lot.
[07:25] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we have prefix and KV cache strategies; you can cache embeddings or token-level KV depending on model support. caching reduces token costs significantly for repeated context.
[07:35] Lena Ortiz: For the benchmark, what data do you need from us besides prompts? environment specs?
[07:40] Diego Alvarez: Sample prompt set, reference outputs if available, preferred languages, and target latency SLOs. optionally a small anonymized dataset for realistic throughput measurement.
[07:49] Priya Nair: We'll prep that. any thoughts on fallback models for graceful degradation if your primary model is oversubscribed?
[07:56] Maya Chen: We recommend a fall-back stack: primary -> quantized variant -> smaller local model. Redwood's router can do automatic fallback by policy.
[08:06] Tom Reynolds: Question about pricing: do you do committed use discounts for Dedicated?
[08:11] Maya Chen: Yes, monthly/annual commits available; committed plans get lower per-token rates and reserved GPU capacity.
[08:18] Ethan Park: For audit and debug, can you trace back model output to the exact model version and prompt used? we need that for incident reports.
[08:24] Diego Alvarez: Absolutely — token-level tracing with model version IDs and route context is included.
[08:30] Priya Nair: Ok one more: model updates and drift detection — do you have quality monitoring?
[08:36] Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. you can set baselines and get alerted on drift.
[08:44] Lena Ortiz: Who would be our day-to-day contact during PoC?
[08:47] Maya Chen: That's me for commercial and Diego for technical. we'll also assign a CSM if we move to Dedicated.
[08:53] Tom Reynolds: sounds good. any blockers for us to start the Hosted PoC this week?
[08:58] Maya Chen: We can spin up Hosted routes quickly; Dedicated benchmark needs scheduling but we can propose next week.
[09:04] Priya Nair: Let's recap next steps — we'll send prompts, you send perf plan and pricing.
[09:10] Maya Chen: Correct. Diego, will you own the test plan?
[09:13] Diego Alvarez: Yes I'll draft it and share.
[09:16] Ethan Park: one last security Q: if we do Hosted for initial tests, will our PHI be excluded from logs by default?
[09:23] Maya Chen: By default Hosted collects telemetry for ops; we can enable log redaction and no-logging for sensitive payloads on enterprise tiers. we'll document exactly how to opt-out.
[09:33] Priya Nair: Great, thanks everyone.
[09:36] Tom Reynolds: Thanks all.
[09:38] Maya Chen: Thanks team, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet, perf plan, and security docs.
[09:43] -- End of meeting --
